method: For each feature in the p1 feature matrix, git log -p on feature/site-revamp (revamp1) and feature/site-revamp2 (revamp2) from their common base 0c8c734f1 to each branch tip; mapped every removed/rewritten artifact to the commit and workflow phase that changed it; classified each loss as (a) deliberate replacement, (b) accidental drop, (c) gate-driven removal; measured additions from the same diffs.

classification_tally.note: several losses are mixed (e.g. app.js layer is deliberate-replacement-of-mechanism + accidental-drop-of-toggle/TOC; rules are gate-driven removal + deliberate replacement). 18 loss entries classified by dominant class. The 6 additional losses (labs corpus, OG metadata, GitHub links, field-map, no-JS fallback, methodology footer) were found by the p5 INDEPENDENT review (separate agent, no prior exposure to the analysis).

key_findings: The interactive-layer loss happened in TWO revamp1 commits: the pages (calculator, charts, levers, tables, narrative depth) in 54201491a (p2_editorial_rewrite), and app.js (theme toggle, statMap, data-anal, TOC) in 80a3bd9af (p3_implementation). Revamp2 inherited all of it.

The calculator + cost chart removals were GATE-DRIVEN (c): the research doc — authored in p0 by the same model (terra) — classified the calculator as 'SaaS-adjacent' and ordered it deleted, with only a vague '[C] explorable' future form that revamp1 never delivered and revamp2 delivered as exactly ONE slider.

The evidence charts + data tables + methodology operator inventory + databricks fold were ACCIDENTAL DROPS (b): not ordered by any research-doc decision, never inventoried, never ported. The revamp's diagram inventory listed only NEW diagrams, so no gate checked for the existing ones.

The revamp1 p4 self-review (docs/reviews/cap_site_revamp_review.md) passed with F7 = ACCEPTED LIMITATION 'no Chromium/Firefox/Node runtime' — the reviewer never rendered the site. The followup's 'deployed site had ZERO visuals' is consistent with a static-source inspection: revamp1's committed HTML has zero inline <svg> (all JS-injected), so a grep finds nothing even though the wiring exists.
Revamp1 deviated from its own spec's hard_rule 1: commits lack the '[workflow] <phase>' prefix, and p2 shipped a broken intermediate tree (pages referencing data-ad slots before app.js v2 existed).

What the revamps ADDED is real: campaign receipts with SHA256s, provenance tags site-wide (57 -> 65 -> 108), question.html, a data-wired diagram system, interactive rule cards, and DOM-verification tooling — the regression is a LOSSLESS-substitution failure, not an absence of new work.

p5 adversarial additions (from the INDEPENDENT review): the revamp data.js dropped the entire labs corpus (build-gate artifact, not editorial); OG/social metadata, GitHub linking (21->2), the field-map image, and methodology's footer were all lost in the same p2 rewrite; and revamp pages degrade to literal 'not loaded' placeholders when JS is off (main hardcodes real numbers in markup).
